1. open the starwars dataset in tidyverse
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data("starwars")
```

2. create a graph showing the frequency of eye colors in the dataset. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(eye_color))+geom_bar()
```

3. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(eye_color))+geom_bar(fill = "gold", color= "maroon")+theme_dark()+ xlab("Eye Color")+ ylab("Frequency")+ggtitle("Eye Color of Star Wars Characters")+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))
#the +theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)) code turns the x axis color labels 90 degrees, moves them to be more in-line with the bars they're under, and aligns the end of the label with the bottom edge of the graph.  
```

4. Create a graph displaying information about character's height in each homeworld. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(homeworld, height))+geom_boxplot()
```

5. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(homeworld, height))+geom_boxplot()+geom_jitter(color="red", alpha = .3)+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))+ xlab("Eye Color")+ ylab("Frequency")+ggtitle("Eye Color of Star Wars Characters")
#the +theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle = 90... code turns the homeworld labels 90 degrees, "vjust=0.5" moves the now vertically aligned homeworld labels to the left slightly, and "hjust=1" aligns the last letter of the homeworld label with the bottom edge of the graph. 
```

6. Create a graph of character's height by mass. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, height))+geom_point()
```

7.Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, height))+geom_point(shape = 17)+ xlab("Mass (kg)")+ ylab("Height (cm) ")+ggtitle("Height by Mass for Star Wars Characters")+theme_light()

```

8. Add gender as a third variable to your graph of height by mass. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, height, color=gender))+geom_point()

```

9. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, height, color=gender))+geom_point()+ xlab("Mass (kg)")+ ylab("Height (cm) ")+ggtitle("Height by Mass for Star Wars Characters")+theme_light()
```
